newsitem.title: SPAIN: Argentaria sets new plan to boost gains.
newsitem.headline: Argentaria sets new plan to boost gains.

text.p: Spain's Group Corporacion Bancaria de Espana (Argentaria) said on Friday it had started a new three-year plan aimed at boosting profitability and reinforcing its presence in the banking sector.

"Profitability on the group's equity capital will increase in a significant form via double-digit year-on-year growth on our (gross) profits," President Francisco Gonzalez told shareholders at the annual general meeting on Friday.

The group plans to boost its profitability on equity capital to 15 percent from the current 10.42 percent. It also wants to lift the yield on shares so that it exceeds that of the 10-year bond which is yielding about seven percent.
The new strategy will have particular emphasis on retail banking where Argentaria plans to cut costs, improve technology and expand client service.
"We want to be the low-cost producer," Gonzalez told journalists after the shareholders meeting.
Innovative technology was the road to achieve that, he said.
Argentaria's domestic loan business fell 4.7 percent to 5.4 trillion pesetas in 1996 and its capital fell 7.2 percent to 3.2 trillion pesetas. Its equity capital is more than 280 billion pesetas.
He rejected the idea of expansion designed to raise short-term profits. He said some Spanish rivals' aggressive Latin American investments would have to "be judged over time."
He added that Argentaria would be looking to an "international alliance in the broadest strategic sense..."
Argentaria has some three percent of Endesa and 5.21 percent in Telefonica.

"We don't want to be an industrial group in the sense of participating actively in management. We would like to raise our stake in Telefonica, but we aren't in a financial position to do so short-term," he said.
The planned sale of the state's remaining 29.2 percent stake in Argentaria would help raise the group's competitive edge.

"A group like Argentaria would lose competitive edge if it continued to have state participation," he said, but added that it would be convenient to form a stable shareholding nucleus before privatisation goes forward.
